cards.name: Sauvignon Blanc
cards.footnote: Always in the glass: grapefruit, lime, green apple, and herbaceous notes from grass to jalapeño.

cards.name: Riesling
cards.headline: The full range, held up by brilliant acidity
cards.footnote: German Rieslings often show a petrol or slate-like minerality that grows with age.

flashCards.title: Three more grapes to know
flashCards.intro: Tap a grape. One card each, in the words of this lesson.

cards.name: Pinot Grigio
cards.text: Light, refreshing wines. In Alsace, as Pinot Gris, it shows fuller body with stone fruit and honey.

cards.name: Viognier
cards.text: Aromatic wines, often with a viscous, almost oily texture despite being dry.

scenario.title: Put it to work
scenario.intro: Reading builds knowledge. Choosing builds judgment.
scenario.prompt: A guest tells you: “I would like a Chardonnay, but nothing oaky or buttery.” Which bottle do you reach for?

choices.feedback: Cool-climate Chablis is lean and mineral-driven, with green apple and citrus instead of vanilla and butter.

choices.text: A California Chardonnay made with oak and malolactic fermentation
choices.feedback: That is the creamy, buttery, vanilla-and-toast style the guest asked you to skip. Chablis is the better call.
Viognier is dry and aromatic, but it is not Chardonnay, and its viscous texture is not what this guest described. Chablis is the better call.

options: Converts sharp malic acid into softer lactic acid
questions.explanation: It converts malic acid into lactic acid, which creates the creamy, buttery character. Vanilla and toast come from oak.

questions.prompt: Which region makes exuberant, tropical Sauvignon Blanc with passion fruit and gooseberry?
questions.explanation: Marlborough, in New Zealand. The Loire Valley makes crisper, more mineral styles.

questions.prompt: Which grape combines citrus and green apple with white pepper?
questions.explanation: Grüner Veltliner, from Austria, known for its distinctive white pepper and herbal qualities.

tryThisWeek.title: Three things to try this week
items: Taste an unoaked and an oaked Chardonnay side by side and look for the color and the mouthfeel differences
Smell a Sauvignon Blanc and look for grapefruit and grass
Open a Riesling and decide: dry or sweet?
